abstract: Extracellular deposition of amyloid plaques is a major hallmark in Alzheimers disease, in which amyloid-beta fibrils are key constituents. Fibrillation of amyloid-beta is modulated by several key sequence motifs, among which the G33LMVG37 motif located in the C-terminal is particularly significant. Moreover, the interaction between amyloid-beta and cellular membrane can be determining factor in its oligomerization. Here, we present membrane scaffold protein encased lipid nanodiscs as a model membrane mimic to investigate the roles of G33 and G37 in membrane-mediated amyloid-beta40 oligomerization. Using a combination of spectroscopic and microscopic techniques, accompanied by molecular dynamic simulations, we demonstrate that these Gly residues are crucial in regulating both self-assembly and membrane-associated oligomerization of amyloid-beta40. We report the formation of structurally distinct amyloid-beta40 oligomers upon interaction with nanodiscs. Our mutational studies reveal a direct involvement of G33 or G37 residues in membrane interaction, leading to prolonged oligomer lifetime.
